content: Start by reading TASK.md, then complete the assignment.

content.content:
1	# Task 3: skinned character with clip crossfade
2	
3	Build a scene with three.js 0.185.1 (`three` and `@types/three`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	The file `/assets/soldier.glb` is a skinned character with animation clips (including `Idle`, `Walk`, `Run`).
6	
7	Requirements:
8	1. Load `/assets/soldier.glb`, scale/position it so the whole character stands on a ground plane and is framed by the camera.
9	2. It starts playing `Idle`.
10	3. Pressing `R` cross-fades to `Run` over 0.4 seconds; pressing `I` cross-fades back to `Idle` over 0.4 seconds.
11	4. One shadow-casting light, shadow on the ground.
12	5. Expose `window.__EVAL__ = { clip: () => string }` returning the name of the clip currently being played (the target clip once a fade starts).
13	
14	The rendering contract in the next section applies. Set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true` after the model has loaded and the first frame is drawn.
15	
16	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
17	
18	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
19	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
20	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
21	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
22	- When you are done, call `

I'm checking that the Soldier.glb model's bounding box computes correctly even as a skinned mesh, and planning to match animation clip names case-insensitively while wiring up keydown listeners and crossfade transitions between actions.

For shadows, I'll set up a directional light with shadow casting enabled, mark character meshes to cast shadows, and have the ground plane receive them.

input.summary:
I wrote `src/main.ts`, and it passes the typecheck. I haven't run `vite build` or opened it in a browser, so none of the behavior below has been checked at runtime. The code loads `/assets/soldier.glb`, scales it to about 1.8 units tall and stands it on a ground plane at the origin. The camera is placed from the model's bounding box to frame the whole character. It starts on `Idle`. Pressing `R` or `I` cross-fades to `Run` or `Idle` over 0.4 s. One directional light casts shadows onto the ground. `window.__EVAL__.clip()` returns the target clip name as soon as a fade starts. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after the model has loaded and the first frame with it has been rendered.

The code assumes the clips are named exactly `Idle` and `Run`, as in the task description, and I didn't inspect the GLB to confirm. It also assumes the soldier faces +z, so the camera sits on the +z side; if the model faces the other way, you'd see its back.
